It is not the codec reading that this fix removes: it happens the same way on a tool that reads links by the plain codec, and the fix only changes what the late write holds (the state shown instead of the codec's reading). Note on behaviour, not a side effect: between a popstate and the reader's next press, key or input inside a [data-frame], no change is written to the bar, even on a page opened without a link. The rule RT-FIX-P4-shared already applied to pages opened from a link now also applies after a popstate. The decisions fragment records this, along with the known limit for asynchronous loads interrupted by a press. I found no tool that changes its state through a control outside [data-frame] other than exampleLoaded (which counts as an action) and no window-level key handler, so no reader move goes unwritten in practice.
